newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds drift lower, market attracts sellers.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds drift lower, market attracts sellers.

text.p: Irish government bonds drifted lower in thin trade on Monday as the market was hit by a touch of profit-taking, dealers said.

"Dublin is a little weaker all round but the long papers were hit the hardest. A spell of profit-taking was inevitable after two bumper weeks for bonds. It's a pretty skimpy week for market-moving data so the market will have to move on its own momentum," one dealer said.
By 1525 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 was down 28p at 107.12 to yield 5.87 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 was 48p weaker at 107.82 to yield 6.77 percent.
"Dublin is at about 86 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year spread after being 72 basis points over bunds at the end of last week," the dealer said.
"The Irish market will be focusing on retail sales data and producer price data in the U.S. on Friday to see how the economy is doing there," he added.
In the UK, gilts lumbered through a consolidation phase after weaker-than-expected UK industrial production data gave a slight filip to the market.
Dublin dealers said it may be one of those weeks when London sets the pace and the Irish market tracks its movements.
London dealers said they expected political factors like the Conservative Party conference to play an important role in UK financial market movements.
